newsitem.title: JAPAN: SESC to file complaint vs Nomura execs soon - paper. [CORRECTED 09:40 GMT]
newsitem.headline: SESC to file complaint vs Nomura execs soon - paper. [CORRECTED 09:40 GMT]

text.p: Japan's securities watchdog plans to file a complaint with prosecutors against former executives of Nomura Securities Co Ltd and Nomura itself as early as Wednesday, the Nihon Keizai Shimbun business daily said over the weekend.
(Corrects to indicate that Nomura itself, not "a corporate racketeer", is reported to be the subject of a planned complaint.)

The Securities and Exchange Surveillance Commission (SESC) raided Nomura's offices in March in a widening probe into the brokerage's role in payments to a corporate client who has been linked to a "sokaiya" racketeer.
Sokaiya typically try to extort money from firms by threatening to expose dubious business practices or to disturb shareholders' meetings.
The former Nomura executives are suspected of illegally providing about 50 million yen of Nomura money to the client.

An SESC spokesman was not immediately available on Monday morning to comment on the report, which appeared in the Saturday edition of the newspaper. Such a complaint is the first step in bringing legal action against a company or an individual.
